stories.summary: Owner-only Jira integration configuration through the shared integration create route and form, storing the site URL and exactly one of a project key or a template project, the API token only as a secret-store reference, the non-secret MCP definition and a not-verified state, rejecting ambiguous targets, non-https sites, blank tokens and credential-bearing MCP definitions, and owning the Jira edit route that preserves the secret and MCP definition, clears the verified time on a target or credential change and requires the test-purpose confirmation

Owner-only source-control configuration extending the shared create route and form with the source-control branch, storing the sandbox repository, base branch and non-secret MCP definition with one integration per project, warning when the repository is also used by a platform project and reporting an unavailable inventory without blocking, rejecting malformed repositories, blank base branches, credential-bearing MCP definitions and a second source-control integration, and leaving source-control editing out of scope

Owner-only AI model profiles extending the shared create route and form with the model branch, a name, vendor, https base URL and a complete high/medium/low tier-to-model mapping, allowing several profiles per project and rejecting missing or unknown tiers, non-https base URLs and duplicate profile names, with the run-purpose list exposing the profile id, name and verified time

Owner-triggered verification per provider that resolves the secret at call time and proves the stored target is usable — the Jira project or template project is readable, the repository is readable with push permission and the base branch exists, and every tier model identifier is available — stamps verified_at on success, leaves the last successful time unchanged on a rejected credential, missing secret or unreachable target, refuses non-owners, treats the time as advisory for run selection, and clears it when an edit changes the target or credential

Credential secrecy across the durable record, settings page, application log and run results: only an opaque secret reference in the integrations row, a masked interface, redacted logs and results through a shared helper that resolves the selected credentials at call time, and an edit that preserves the stored secret and MCP definition and requires the test-purpose confirmation

Test-purpose attestation required on every integration save, recorded as test_only in config with unconfirmed saves refused, and unconfirmed integrations excluded from the run-purpose integration list that run start consumes
